About the Role
We are looking for an Entry-Level Software Engineer to design, develop, and maintain software solutions with guidance from experienced engineers. This full-time, remote position is suited to individuals beginning their software engineering careers who are eager to learn, adapt to new technologies, and contribute to software development projects.
You will write clean and efficient code, participate in code reviews, debug and resolve issues, and contribute to back-end web services and APIs. You will also collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand project requirements, document technical work, and assist with software testing and deployment activities.
Key Responsibilities
Design, develop, and maintain software solutions under the guidance of experienced engineers.
Write clean, efficient, and maintainable code.
Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback from other engineers.
Debug software issues and contribute to their resolution.
Assist with developing and maintaining back-end web services and APIs.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand requirements and contribute to project solutions.
Document technical work and development processes.
Assist with software testing and deployment activities.
Continue learning and adapting to new technologies and software engineering practices.
Required Qualifications
Foundational knowledge of computer science, including algorithms, data structures, and software engineering principles.
Knowledge of software development and programming, with experience in at least one modern programming language such as Java, C#, Python, or JavaScript.
Understanding of object-oriented programming (OOP) concepts and their practical application.
Exposure to back-end web development, including APIs, databases, and server-side frameworks.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Ability to work remotely, manage time effectively, and collaborate using online communication and project management tools.
Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and willingness to learn through feedback and mentorship.
Preferred Qualifications
Basic knowledge of version control systems such as Git.
Familiarity with software development lifecycle practices.

China produces about 85% of the world's cathode active material. The West needs new battery chemistries to compete, but traditional R&D can take years to deliver them. 
 
Today, we announced $45M in funding to change that. 
 
Backed by  Zone II Ventures, and Course Corrected, we're scaling our AI-powered Discovery Engine, which combines 18 years of proprietary battery data with automated labs that physically build and test new materials. Over these 18 years our platform has run more than 225 projects for more than 85 customers across the battery value chain, including nearly a dozen Fortune 500 companies, and has resulted in more than 100 battery patents.  Along the way, the platform generated an internally consistent dataset covering more than 500,000 physical cells tested at over 165 million cycles.  
 
Our technology has already helped deliver DRX, a new family of nickel- and cobalt-free cathode materials designed to reduce dependence on China. Now, we're bringing DRX toward commercialization while using AI to accelerate the next generation of breakthroughs. 
 
Led by founder and CEO Mathias Ingvarsson, COO and former Tesla manufacturing leader Steven Prast, and Chief Scientific Officer Dee Strand, we're building a faster path from battery discovery to commercial deployment. 
 
Read more in Fortune by Nick Lichtenberg. Article link in the first comment.

BREAKING: Brookfield announces HUGE $27 BILLION AI data centre project in the UK! 

Brookfield has partnered with British energy company Drax Group and AI business Radiant to develop one of the UK’s largest AI data centres at Drax Power Station in the north of England. 

Bloomberg reports that the project could attract more than $27 Billion billion in investment, with an initial $3.3 Billion planned for the first phase, backed by Brookfield’s partnership with the Qatar Investment Authority.

The idea is to build the data centre alongside an existing power station, giving it access to the enormous amounts of electricity needed to run AI technology. Drax CEO Will Gardiner said: “If constructed in full, this project could become one of the largest data centres in the UK.” Brookfield's Connor Teskey recently said of AI infrastructure: "there is no shortage of capital - and there is no shortage of demand."

Big news for European AI infrastructure!

Follow Joseph Cass for finance news and insights.

Clarification: On Thursday, Oct. 15, thousands of Aggie students took part in TWO major marches to downtown Greensboro:

- The first was a March to the Polls, as previously described, which went from campus to the Union Square polling location downtown on the first day of early voting in North Carolina. Students marched back to campus after voting in protest of the Guilford County Elections Board's removal of their campus early voting polling location earlier this year.

- The second was a March for Justice for Nolan Wells, the 18-year-old young man who tragically died July 4 under murky circumstances in the waters off Mississippi’s Horn Island after celebrating the Independence Day holiday. The march was organized by the A&T chapter of the NAACP, and a coalition of groups worked tirelessly to bring students together in solidarity for Nolan from across campus and the entire state. The march began at A&T’s February One monument, went downtown to the International Civil Rights Museum and returned to campus.

Incredibly, thousands of Aggies took part in *both* marches, but in the video posted here, were returning from the second march, which concluded later. In both instances, outstanding civic leadership and participation were on full display from A&T students in the best tradition of Aggies, who have been leading in important community events since the university’s establishment in 1891. 

A&T continues to be America's largest HBCU, as well as its top-rated public HBCU in Forbes and US News & World Report.

At 20:05 UTC on October 29, approximately USD 6.36 billion began moving out of Binance wallets across ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes. It is the largest crypto theft on record, roughly four times the Bybit hack of February 2025.

TRM Labs attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s elite state-sponsored hacking unit, based on robust on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The same group was named by the FBI in the Bybit hack, and the staging, the Tornado Cash funding and the pre-signed transactions all match earlier North Korea-linked heists.

The response has been fast. Tether, Circle, Ripple, World Liberty Financial and Arbitrum’s Security Council have frozen roughly USD 2.7 billion. But the attacker still controls about USD 2.4 billion in assets beyond any issuer’s reach, and is racing to convert and move them.

TRM continues to work with Binance and the Beacon Network to track the funds and alert partners in real time. The story is still developing, and we will share more as the investigation unfolds.
